talk_track.claim: "We've reserved an HP MJF 1200. No payment needed, plus we get 20% off parts and up to $10,000 in credit."
talk_track.counter: Take the offer seriously, it is a good one. Then ask the question it avoids: the machine does not ship until early 2027. What are they producing between now and then? The 20% parts discount routes their volume to HP's own service bureau, so for the next two quarters they are outsourcing production and building a dependency, not building a capability. The credit is only redeemable against a machine that does not exist yet. Ask what happens to the credit if the ship date slips.

talk_track.claim: "HP is everywhere. Their marketing is far ahead of yours."
talk_track.counter: Be precise instead of defensive. HP runs 13 creatives on one platform, 24 live instances, and 97% of its biggest flight landed in the United States. What it does well is concentrate: one teaser took 500K-1M impressions in nineteen days around a launch. That is a burst strategy, not superior always-on marketing, and it is buyable. Meanwhile three of its live ads carry expired dates, including an Open House that ended Oct 1. Volume is not rigor.

talk_track.claim: “HP's IF 600 HT is open materials, no lock-in.”
talk_track.counter: Open materials also means unvalidated materials. Ask who certifies the process for their application, and who they call when a build fails qualification.

talk_track.claim: “HP is the drone additive manufacturing leader.”
talk_track.counter: HP has no drone ad on LinkedIn today. The webinars that named Blueflite, Unusual Machines and Firestorm Labs were removed between Oct 12 and Oct 30. That was a proof set, not a market, and it is no longer being advertised. Ask for production volumes, and ask what HP is offering drone teams now.

talk_track.claim: “HP is everywhere in additive right now.”
talk_track.counter: HP runs 13 creatives on one platform, LinkedIn, and zero on Meta [Meta not checked, so say 'not found']. Its April teaser and February booth ad are still live in October. That is a narrow, under-maintained program, not omnipresence.
